frequency_question: How often does Congress successfully pass a joint resolution of disapproval to block a submitted 123 agreement?
membership_rule: Includes all formal 123 nuclear cooperation agreements transmitted by the executive branch to Congress under the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 as amended. Excludes peaceful nuclear cooperation agreements that did not trigger formal congressional review periods or where no resolution of disapproval was formally introduced and voted upon.

cases.name: U.S.-Iran Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action related nuclear review framework (analogy for contentious Middle East agreements)

provenance_note: claims 30 cases from only 3 named (10.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 30 named or categorized; complete historical enumeration of 123 agreements yields zero successful congressional blocks.
known_gaps: While dozens of 123 agreements have entered into force quietly, high-stakes geopolitical iterations (like potential Middle East pacts) face intense rhetoric but have never successfully cleared the veto override threshold.
skeleton: Total formal 123 agreements submitted since 1978 (~25-30 agreements), divided into routine civilian agreements versus highly contentious geopolitical agreements subject to bipartisan legislative friction.
multiplier: 0 successful blocks out of approximately 30 total submitted agreements over 48 years.
validity_reason: The statutory framework of the Atomic Energy Act and the high institutional bar for overriding a presidential veto remain stable across administrations.
